evals.prompt: A user asks: 'the login page is broken after yesterday's deploy'. Decide which skill applies and why.
evals.expected_output: Correct routing through the decision tree with the chosen skill and rationale
expectations: The chosen skill matches the decision tree in the meta-skill
The rationale references the routing logic rather than guessing
Core operating behaviors (assumptions surfaced) are respected

evals.prompt: Route a new production feature from a vague request through specification, planning, implementation, pull-request review, merge, and release. State the ordered lifecycle, the skill owner at each phase, when the PR is created and marked ready, and the artifact or evidence that permits each transition.
evals.expected_output: One coherent feature lifecycle from discovery through release with explicit owners, artifacts, revision-scoped gates, and cross-cutting disciplines
expectations: The happy path is ordered as discovery/definition, specification, planning, draft PR, incremental TDD build, feature verification, ready PR, merge review, merge, and production shipping
The route distinguishes /test as the focused TDD entry point from /verify as assembled-feature validation

The draft PR is created within the authorized endpoint after checked, scope-authorized spec and plan artifacts, while readiness requires current-revision verification. Routine phase transitions reuse authorization; human input is reserved for unresolved critical decisions or enforced approval.

The response names the branch-scoped docs/tracks/<track-id>/ bundle, using NNN-name ids and including spec.md or bug.md, plan.md, todo.md, PR context, verification.md, review.md, and ship.md release/rollback evidence; canonical specs remain capability-based and are reconciled before review
Git, CI, security, documentation, and observability are treated as cross-cutting disciplines rather than late cleanup

evals.prompt: The assembled feature fails an acceptance-criterion check during /verify. Explain the exact workflow from that failure until the PR can become ready, without treating debugging as the normal verification phase or quietly changing scope.
evals.expected_output: A failure-path route that records evidence, enters systematic debugging, applies a test-first fix, and returns to full verification on the new revision before PR readiness
expectations: The failed verification result is preserved as evidence and the readiness verdict remains FAIL or INCOMPLETE
The route enters debugging-and-error-recovery only because a check failed
A behavioral fix uses RED-GREEN-REFACTOR and updates the plan/spec only if scope or acceptance criteria genuinely changed
Focused checks are followed by /verify again on the new revision
/pr ready remains blocked until current-revision verification evidence is complete
